title: NCLEX Buddy
disclaimer: Practice questions are original NCLEX-style teaching items created for this app. The listed links are study references and are not copied into the question bank.

questions.prompt: Four clients call for assistance at the same time. Which client should the nurse assess first?
options: A client 2 hours after thyroidectomy who reports tingling around the mouth
A client with pneumonia who needs help repositioning in bed
A client with diabetes who requests a bedtime snack
A client after knee arthroplasty who rates incisional pain as 6 out of 10
questions.rationale: Perioral tingling after thyroidectomy can indicate hypocalcemia from parathyroid injury and may progress to laryngospasm or seizures.
questions.teachingPoint: Use airway risk and rapid deterioration when several needs compete.

questions.prompt: A client taking digoxin has nausea, blurred yellow vision, and a heart rate of 52 beats/min. What is the nurse's best action?
options: Hold the digoxin and notify the provider
Encourage the client to ambulate before the dose
questions.rationale: Bradycardia and visual changes are warning signs of digoxin toxicity.
questions.teachingPoint: Check pulse and toxicity cues before giving cardiac glycosides.

questions.prompt: Which infection-control action is most appropriate before entering the room of a client with suspected Clostridioides difficile infection?
options: Wear gloves and gown and plan to wash hands with soap and water after care
Wear a surgical mask and use alcohol hand sanitizer after care
Place the client in a positive-pressure room
Use sterile gloves for all contact with the client
questions.rationale: Clostridioides difficile infection requires contact precautions, and spores are best removed with soap and water.
questions.teachingPoint: Match precautions to the organism and transmission route.
